title: A defined research investigation
explanation: A study establishes the context in which participants, observations and procedures have meaning. Treat its identifier as part of your data's scope rather than as a display-only label.

title: The plan behind the data
explanation: The protocol describes the intended investigation. An application schema implements selected operational needs; it does not replace the protocol or prove that every procedure happened.

title: The participant represented in records
explanation: Here, subject refers to the fictional participant to whom records relate. Our identifiers are invented; no person can be looked up from them.

title: A study's operational location context
explanation: A site identifies where study activities are organized. A site-local participant label may collide with a label elsewhere, so identity design needs explicit scope.

title: A grouping of study activities
explanation: A visit can organize related activities, but planned and actual activity timing need not coincide. Do not derive observation dates solely from a visit schedule.

title: Electronic case report form
explanation: An eCRF collects a chosen set of study information. A form is a collection interface; its fields need not map one-to-one to output columns or datasets.

title: Electronic data capture
explanation: EDC software supports collecting and managing study data. Its operational records and exports serve different tasks and may use different structures.

title: History of recorded changes
explanation: An audit history makes changes attributable and inspectable. A current-value export alone usually cannot explain who changed a record or why.

title: A question about recorded data
explanation: A data query flags an issue needing clarification. Closing a query is a workflow event, not automatically proof that every downstream representation is correct.

title: An organization and a family of standards
explanation: CDISC develops standards for clinical research data. Name the particular standard and version rather than treating CDISC as a single file format.

title: A data-collection standards context
explanation: CDASH addresses collection standardization. This curriculum only introduces its relationship to later representations; it does not reproduce collection specifications.

title: An exchange-oriented standard
explanation: ODM is relevant to structured clinical data exchange. It is distinct from a table of observations, and this site does not implement an ODM reader or writer.

title: A model for tabular study data
explanation: SDTM provides a conceptual organization for study data. Our lessons illustrate selected structures without supplying the complete normative model.

title: An implementation guide
explanation: An SDTM implementation guide adds context for applying the model. Record its version separately; the number is not the model version.

title: A group of related observations
explanation: A domain gives a dataset a subject-matter context. Its identity is not necessarily the same as a screen, form or operational database table.

title: An attribute in a representation
explanation: A variable gives a column meaning. Knowing its name does not by itself establish its allowed values, requiredness or derivation.

title: Something represented about a subject
explanation: An observation is a useful unit for reasoning about repeated measurements or occurrences. First ask what one output row represents.

title: A value used to distinguish entities
explanation: An identifier should preserve its exact representation and scope. A numeric-looking identifier is not necessarily a number suitable for arithmetic.

title: Values governed by a vocabulary
explanation: Controlled terminology helps make categorical values interpretable across systems. Its release and applicable list matter alongside the dataset structure.

title: A particular grouping of terms
explanation: A codelist defines a vocabulary context. A concept existing in a terminology service does not by itself prove membership in the list needed for your variable.

title: The representation used in an output
explanation: A submission value is distinct from a human-friendly label or concept code. This edition does not bundle approved lists or assert that its invented tokens are submission values.

title: Information describing the data
explanation: Metadata explains structure and interpretation: what a field means, how it is represented, and where it came from. An example value is not a substitute for that description.

title: A dataset-description standard
explanation: Define-XML is relevant to describing datasets and their metadata. We link to standards context but do not generate or validate submission documents.

title: Records invented for a demonstration
explanation: Our records originate as fictional examples, not from real participants with identifying fields removed. Synthetic does not mean clinically valid or submission-ready.
